identity.title: VTE risk history (Wells items): immobilization >=3 days or surgery within 4-12 weeks, prior objectively confirmed VTE, active malignancy

technique.how: Ask directly for each Wells item: bed rest >=3 days or major surgery within the past 4 weeks (12 weeks for PE rules); prior DVT/PE confirmed by imaging; cancer under active treatment, treated within 6 months, or palliative. Record each item as present/absent rather than a global impression.
technique.prerequisites: Patient or collateral informant able to give a history; access to prior records improves accuracy for confirmed VTE.

interpretation.positive_finding: Any single item roughly doubles the odds of DVT (pooled LR+ 1.8-2.7) and modestly raises the odds of PE (LR+ 1.6-2.1); items are meant to be summed within the Wells score, where high probability carries LR ~5 and DVT prevalence ~53%.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of individual risk factors does not exclude VTE (item-level LR- near 1); only a low overall Wells score (LR ~0.25, DVT prevalence ~5%) plus a negative D-dimer safely excludes DVT.
interpretation.pitfalls: Pooled item LRs have substantial heterogeneity; patients often under-report remote surgery or immobilization, and 'prior DVT' should be objectively confirmed rather than self-diagnosed. Do not treat any single item as a rule-in.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive items move the Wells score toward moderate/high: order compression US (DVT) or CTPA/imaging (PE); no items plus low score allows D-dimer-based exclusion.

sources.citation: Goodacre S, Sutton AJ, Sampson FC. Meta-analysis: the value of clinical assessment in the diagnosis of deep venous thrombosis. Ann Intern Med. 2005;143(2):129-139.
West J, Goodacre S, Sampson F. The value of clinical features in the diagnosis of acute pulmonary embolism: systematic review and meta-analysis. QJM. 2007;100(12):763-769.
Wells PS, Owen C, Doucette S, Fergusson D, Tran H. Does this patient have deep vein thrombosis? JAMA. 2006;295(2):199-207.
Chunilal SD, Eikelboom JW, Attia J, et al. Does this patient have pulmonary embolism? JAMA. 2003;290(21):2849-2858.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never use absence of risk factors alone to stop a VTE work-up in a patient with unexplained dyspnea, hypoxia, or syncope; ~30% of PE occurs without identifiable provoking factors.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hemodynamic instability with any VTE risk factor warrants immediate bedside echo/CTPA and consideration of empiric anticoagulation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Item-level pooled LRs showed substantial statistical heterogeneity across cohorts (Goodacre 2005; West 2008); definitions of 'recent' surgery/immobilization vary between studies.

extraction_notes: Item-level LRs taken from abstracts of the Goodacre 2005 (DVT) and West 2008 (PE) meta-analyses; full text/tables were not accessible so 95% CIs and LR- values for individual items are null (partially_quantified). Only rule-in direction is reported for these items. The 2003 PE RCE (Chunilal) and 2006 DVT RCE (Wells) abstracts report performance of gestalt/prediction rules, not individual items; the 2006 RCE gives DVT prevalence 5% low vs 53% high Wells probability, cited here as context. Anand 1998 RCE abstract contains no item-level numbers. Verifier: check Goodacre 2005 Table 2 for CIs and LR- per item.
